said that phase 3 data for Caplyta (lumateperone) showed the atypical antipsychotic led to rapid reduction in manic symptoms compared to placebo at week 3 in adults with bipolar I disorder.
that those on Caplyta had a 4.8-point greater reduction in Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) total score — the primary endpoint — compared to placebo. Also, improvement was seen as early as day 3.
A key secondary endpoint, Clinical Global Impression–Severity (CGI-S) score, a measure of overall illness severity, was also met.
Caplyta is already approved for bipolar I and II depressive episodes.

title: J&J sees positive late-stage data for Caplyta in reducing bipolar manic symptoms
